o: The tree has exactly three nodes: a root with a left and a right child. We simply return whether root.val equals left.val + right.val. Example [10,4,6] gives 10 == 4+6 -> true; [5,3,1] gives 5 != 4 -> false. Constraints are trivial; no traversal strategy is needed beyond direct child access.
k: Direct field access suffices since the shape is fixed at three nodes.
Values can be negative, but simple addition/comparison handles that automatically.

a.i: Read the three values and compare the root's value to the sum of its children. Nothing else is required.
s: Return whether their sum equals root.val.
a.t: O(1) — constant number of node accesses.

w: This is a warm-up; just avoid overcomplicating it with recursion. A possible follow-up asks the same question for a general tree, which becomes a simple recursive check over all internal nodes.
